text: Bounded ERP policy: confirmed nonrecoverable purchase tax is included in inventory or expense cost. Inventory purchases and operating expenses have different debit roles. No VAT-style recoverable input-tax asset is assumed. IRS small-business tax guidance is a reference, not a GAAP certification or a jurisdiction engine.

IRS guidance distinguishes sales tax imposed on the buyer from tax imposed on the seller. Buyer tax collected for government is excluded from income. This pilot's explicit buyer-tax case credits OUTPUT_TAX separately from SALES. Seller-imposed taxes require a different policy and are outside this pilot.

Confirmed no-tax sale: credit SALES, debit evidenced payments and any receivable. Perpetual inventory also debits COGS and credits INVENTORY when cost is recognized. A no-tax fact does not prove exemption.

A later supplier payment debits ACCOUNTS_PAYABLE and credits the evidenced payment account. A later customer receipt debits the payment account and credits ACCOUNTS_RECEIVABLE. Do not recognize tax or revenue a second time.

Transfer own cash to bank: debit BANK, credit CASH. Withdraw bank funds to own cash: debit CASH, credit BANK. Neither transfer is revenue, an expense or a taxable sale. These role proposals do not execute bank transfers.

California provides jurisdiction-specific sales/use-tax rules. Resale documentation, place of use and the taxpayer affect treatment. This source illustrates why a single US rate or automatic tax applicability must not be inferred from a product name. Use tax accrual and seller-imposed sales tax are outside the implemented posting policy.
